explanations: FileSegmentStore.open passes range.endExclusive as fs.createReadStream's `end` option, but `end` is inclusive. The interface (and InMemorySegmentStore's subarray) treat endExclusive as one past the last byte, so the file-backed store returns one extra byte for every ranged read. The handler has already sent Content-Length = endExclusive - start, so the body overruns the declared length, which corrupts responses or causes players/proxies to reject or misalign segments. It only shows up in production (file store), not in tests using the in-memory store. The fix is `end: range.endExclusive - 1`.

For a suffix range (empty first group) the code computes start = Math.max(0, size - suffix) = max(0, -200) = 0 and endExclusive = size = 300. It is not rejected (only suffix 0 is invalid), start is clamped so it is never negative, and null is only returned when there is no header.

parseRange needs meta.sizeBytes to interpret open-ended and suffix ranges and to build Content-Range; headers must be written before the body is piped, and a null stat gives a clean 404. open() streams rather than buffers in the file store, there is no locking, and both stat() and open() go through resolve(), so traversal is checked in both.

parseRange turns the inclusive header end into endExclusive = lastInclusive + 1, and the handler converts back with `range.endExclusive - 1` for the Content-Range header. Stores receive the interface's half-open range; put() only stores data and does no range conversion.
